scope: Sampled browser allocations during an injected independent-array PLY-3 restore; not a production change or passing resource acceptance.
method: The isolated server used the same no-numeric-reuse and fractional-seed bundle modifications as the prior allocation experiment. Chrome DevTools heap sampling started after full export/download and sampled every three seconds during GUI reopen, with a 1048576-byte interval. No explicit garbage collection was requested. The bundle's sampled function lv is the numeric transport unpacker, identified by its scanforge-numeric-transport-v1 validation and matching source structure.
observed: GUI reopen, geometry checks and post-reopen Undo/Redo completed. The guarded job nevertheless failed because its reported peak exceeded 4 GiB by 208896 bytes. The driver exited zero, all owned processes closed, and the temporary download was removed.
limitations: Heap sampling is statistical and measures sampled JavaScript allocations after sampling began; it does not cover all renderer, browser or GPU memory.
Profiling changes the workload, and the amount attributed to the unpacker does not establish which allocation caused the job peak.
A completed lifecycle with an over-limit guard is not a passing resource result or proof that seeded allocation alone caused any difference.
The production restore ownership, native comparisons and milestone gates remain open.
